skill.name: agile-product-owner
skill.description: Agile product ownership toolkit for creating INVEST-compliant user stories, acceptance criteria, sprint plans, backlog priorities, and capacity summaries.
skill.summary: Create user stories, acceptance criteria, and sprint plans for agile backlog work.
skill.author: alirezarezvani

content.user_title: Create Agile Stories and Sprint Plans
content.value_statement: Product teams often lose time turning ideas into clear, testable backlog items. This skill helps create user stories, acceptance criteria, estimates, and capacity-based sprint plans.
actual_capabilities: Generates persona-based user stories in the standard narrative format.
Creates acceptance criteria with Given-When-Then style checks.
Checks generated stories against the INVEST criteria.
Estimates story points using feature complexity indicators.
Plans sprint commitments from backlog priority, story size, and capacity.
Prints backlog summaries with story counts, total points, and priority breakdowns.
limitations: The included command-line script uses a sample epic unless it is edited or imported.
It does not connect to Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps, or other planning systems.
Story estimates are heuristic and need team review before commitment.
It does not track live sprint progress, burndown charts, or delivery history.

use_cases.title: Refine Product Backlogs
use_cases.description: Turn feature ideas into user stories with acceptance criteria and priority guidance.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sprint Planning
use_cases.description: Select committed and stretch stories that fit a planned sprint capacity.

use_cases.title: Review Story Quality
use_cases.description: Check story size, testability, and clarity before work enters development.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a user story for {feature} for {persona}. Include acceptance criteria and a story point estimate.

prompt_templates.title: Break Down Epic
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this epic into INVEST-compliant stories: {epic_description}. Include personas, priorities, estimates, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a sprint with {capacity} story points from this backlog: {backlog}. Show committed stories, stretch goals, and utilization.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this release backlog for INVEST quality, estimation risk, dependencies, and sprint planning concerns: {release_backlog}.

output_examples.input: Create a story for exporting dashboard data.
output: User Story: As a power user, I want to export dashboard data so that I can share analysis with my team.
Acceptance criteria include successful export, input validation, clear error messages, and keyboard access.

output_examples.input: Plan a sprint with 30 points of capacity.
output: Committed work: 28 points across the highest priority stories.
Stretch work: one lower priority story if capacity remains.

output_examples.input: Review a story for INVEST quality.
output: The story is valuable, estimable, and testable.
It may be too large if it includes reporting, sharing, and automation in one item.
Split the work before sprint commitment.

best_practices: Review generated stories with the team before adding them to a sprint.
Keep each story focused on one user outcome and one testable workflow.
Use capacity output as planning guidance, not as a delivery guarantee.
anti_patterns: Committing generated estimates without team discussion.
Using one large story to cover several unrelated product outcomes.
Treating sample epic output as production backlog data without editing it.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates user stories, acceptance criteria, story point estimates, sprint plans, and backlog summaries.

faq.question: Does it follow INVEST criteria?
faq.answer: Yes. The script checks independence, negotiability, value, estimability, size, and testability for generated stories.

faq.question: Can it plan sprint capacity?
faq.answer: Yes. It can select committed and stretch stories based on priority, estimates, and a capacity value.

faq.question: Does it integrate with planning tools?
faq.answer: No. It does not connect directly to Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps, or similar tools.

faq.question: Are the estimates final?
faq.answer: No. Estimates are heuristic and should be reviewed by the delivery team.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
